Every last proper prefix omits one vertex v≠0 and sends it to one of four retained vertices, so the sixteen witness ratios cover every ordering and every such map. For omissions 1,2,3 the witnesses are always 2 or 1+t; for omission 4 they include 1+t, 2, 2/t and (1+t)/t. All these ratios are at least 1+t for t≤1 and at least 2/t for 1≤t≤2. The exhibited maps fix their prefixes, and checking adjacent compositions r_{j-1}r_j=r_{j-1} gives full commutativity by iteration and range nesting. For t≤1 the only enlarged graph edge is 3–4 under r_3, with image length 1+t. For t≥1 the unit-edge images have length at most 1 and the closing edge images have length at most 2, so the bound is max(1,2/t). Edge bounds extend along shortest paths even after the closing edge ceases to be geodesic at t=4. The identity gives the lower bound 1. The linearized retraction has norm equal to its Lipschitz constant by testing canonical molecules and using the free-space universal property; the commuting nested projections induce a basis, not an assertion about all linear bases.
